newsitem.title: USA: Court rejects California, Arizona immigration suits.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects California, Arizona immigration suits.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Tuesday dismissed lawsuits by the states of California and Arizona demanding reimbursement from the U.S. government for the costs of illegal immigration.

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, in a written decision released in San Francisco, said the state of California's claims raised "political questions" which fell outside the jurisdiction of the courts.
It said it dismissed a similar lawsuit by Arizona on the same grounds.
California Gov. Pete Wilson vowed to appeal.

"This is a ground-breaking case that raises novel legal issues which we knew would have to be decided by the United States Supreme Court," Wilson said in a statement. "We are now in a position to seek that review from the High Court."
Arizona's attorney general also planned to appeal the decision, spokeswoman Karie Dozer said.
Both California and Arizona sought to force the U.S. government to reimburse them for the costs of providing education and other services to illegal immigrants.

The lawsuits were similar to those brought by Texas, Florida, New York and New Jersey, Justice Department spokeswoman Carole Florman said. The federal government has prevailed in all of these cases except for Texas, which has not been decided yet, she said.
In its 1994 lawsuit, California asserted that the number of permanent illegal residents it had stood at 1.7 million -- five percent of the state's population.

California estimated that it spent $395 million a year providing emergency health care to illegal aliens, $390 million on incarceration and parole supervision of illegal aliens and $1.5 billion educating illegal immigrants.
California has alleged that the federal government has violated its obligation to protect the state's borders against illegal immigration.
A federal trial court in 1995 dismissed the lawsuit. In Tuesday's decision, the court of appeals affirmed dismissal of the state's lawsuit.

"The concerns expressed by California are unquestionably beyond the authority of the judicial branch," the appeals panel said. It added that the reimbursement sought by California was barred by the Constitution.
Arizona's case, which called for repayment of education and prison expenses, was dismissed on the same grounds, the appeals court said.
